Subject: Atlas Retail — quick help: hosted API baseline & competitor parity

Team,

Atlas (Maya Singh) is asking for a hosted-API baseline + a head-to-head rate comparison vs OpenAI/Anthropic/Together/AWS. They said they have a competing quote from OpenAI that looks like: $0.03 per 1K input tokens / $0.12 per 1K output tokens (guesstimate from procurement). Atlas is a fast-growth retail chain — potential first-year volume ~350M tokens.

Can you help with two things by EOD?
1) A short table of public/observed comparable rates for the vendors above (callouts for embeddings vs text-gen where relevant).
2) A suggested rate-match / promotional offer we can present (margin floor and one-off credit ideas).

I've attached Atlas requirements and a blank competitive sheet — please drop numbers into the sheet and flag any redlines (SOC2 request, data residency, SLA asks).

Aim: keep Redwood hosted offer competitive but preserve 15-20% margin relative to their committed TCO target. If we can present a 3-month pilot credit (e.g. $25k) + a 12-month committed pricing tier, that might close.

Thanks — Priyom

Subject: Re: Atlas Retail — quick help: hosted API baseline & competitor parity

Priyom — adding market color (quick bullets, pulled from recent deals + public docs):
- OpenAI: per-unit published for inference varies by model; for comparable chat/text workloads customers are seeing effective blended prices between $0.02–$0.05 /1K input and $0.08–$0.16 /1K output depending on model & context length. They often bundle volume discounts and credits in RFPs.
- Anthropic: slightly cheaper on some large-chat models if you accept higher latency/limited streaming; ballpark ~$0.015–$0.04 /1K input + $0.06–$0.12 /1K output for committed tiers.
- Together/other smaller providers: aggressive on list price for new logos — can undercut by 10–30% but fewer enterprise features (SLA/KMS).
- AWS Bedrock: typically higher list price but enterprise comfort (VPC, IAM) — deals include infra credits or multi-year discounts.

Notes: the number you quoted for OpenAI looks within the market band. Biggest lever for us: commit term + committed token volume. For Atlas-size volumes (350M tokens/yr) we can propose a tiered discount that gets them to the mid-point of the OpenAI quote while preserving kernel margins.

I'll prepare a quick draft offer:
- 12-month commitment (350M tokens/year), tiered pricing: $0.028/1K input, $0.095/1K output (effective blended ~ $0.05/1K tokens).
- $25k pilot credit applied to first invoice (to offset migration/dev).
- SOC2 attestation + standard Private Data Addendum (no extra cost).

If we need to be more aggressive we could move to $0.025 /1K input with a $20k margin haircut; need Vivek sign-off.

V

Thanks Maya (cc'd internally).

Drafting a one-pager and competitor bullets now — adding the callouts Tableau: latency 95th ~120ms on our hosted tier for 8k context, streaming available, KMS support, and RTO SLA options for Dedicated.

Proposed quick table (to put into the one-pager):
- Redwood Hosted: base list price: $0.045 /1K tokens (no commit), proposed committed: $0.028 /1K input, $0.095 /1K output for Atlas (12m).
- OpenAI (public/procured value): blended observed $0.03-$0.12 /1K depending on model & custom pricing.
- Anthropic: competitive on price for chat; caveat: limited streaming ergonomics.
- Together: price-lead for new logos; fewer enterprise compliance docs.
- AWS Bedrock: enterprise integration strength; pricing often offset by infra credits.

I'll attach the polished one-pager to respond to Maya. Also added a short legal blurb for data retention (30 days for raw logs unless otherwise specified, production observability metrics retained 90 days; retention terms negotiable for enterprise).
